item.title: Pope Leo XIV: In age of AI, the family is the first school of humanity
item.description:
# Pope Leo XIV: In age of AI, the family is the first school of humanity At the same time, the Holy Father underscored, the rapid development of artificial intelligence risks creating new forms of technological dependence, with poorer nations increasingly reliant on wealthier ones.
## The family as the first school of humanity With this in mind, he said that artificial intelligence "must never be allowed to erode this primary cell of society — whether by reducing persons and relationships to data and simulations, by flooding young minds with content that distorts desire, or by economic models that make family life economically precarious."
## Strengthen marriage and families "Dear friends, the world does not need an artificial intelligence that diminishes humanity; rather," Pope Leo insisted, "it needs human intelligence enlightened by wisdom, political authority guided by conscience and technological innovation directed by charity."
Only then, he said, will artificial intelligence become not a rival to humanity but a servant of the common good.

item.title: What Role Will Artificial Intelligence Play in Genitourinary Oncology?
item.description:
# 30. What Role Will Artificial Intelligence Play in Genitourinary Oncology? In the newest episode of _Oncology Decoded_, hosts Manojkumar Bupathi, MD, MS, and Benjamin Garmezy, MD, spoke about the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI)–based tools and large language models (LLMs) into the study and management of genitourinary malignancies.
The conversation helped differentiate between modalities like LLMs, which assist with documentation, chart summarization, and clinical trial matching, and multimodal AI, a tool that involves combining genomics, laboratory values, and other data to generate patient-level insights.

item.title: Drexel's artificial intelligence major enters an uncertain future
item.description:
# Drexel's artificial intelligence major enters an uncertain future Aug. 21, 2026
This fall, Drexel University plans to welcome its first class of students majoring in [Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning](https://drexel.edu/academics/grad-professional-programs/cci/artifical-intelligence-and-machine-learning).
Will a major like this last?
Small—or even larger—companies utilizing AI for advertisements, “artists” generating songs to be used on TikTok and streamed on music platforms, and entry-level job positions being replaced with AI are all real-life examples of how businesses are increasingly turning to AI to churn out work faster. Even terms like “ [A.I. brain fry](https://www.npr.org/2026/04/13/nx-s1-5780867/you-might-be-suffering-from-ai-brain-fry)” have emerged, a state of mind in which someone has cognitive overload due to excessive use of artificial intelligence.
Whether you like it or not, AI has become a crucial part of some workplace settings around the globe. With its growing use, the pace at which businesses operate has accelerated, creating new expectations for how fast employees should complete certain tasks. This is where opinions on AI become more complex and nuanced for some – knowing that AI has its detriments to current society while also acknowledging that it will only continue to advance and may be utilized even more in years to come. Data collected in 2025 shows that [91 percent of businesses plan to increase AI implementation](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/all-in-on-ai-91-of-global-executives-are-scaling-up-ai-efforts-302422567.html) into their companies, suggesting that AI is not simply a trend but a way for companies to take something they deem useful and rearrange their organizational structures in response to it.
Tracing this all back to Drexel’s new Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning major, is it truly smart to implement a major like this?
Pair this with data center anger, worry for the future behavior of society, and the concern of artificial intelligence being able to train future models by storing human and personal thoughts (considering that [approximately up to 54 percent of people, according to a study done by George Mason University, use AI as a way to regulate emotions and store personal thoughts](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/1-in-3-psychologists-say-their-patients-use-ai-as-a-second-therapist/)—which is, interestingly, a very complicated opinion for another day.
